AnswerOption.description: An answer the interface offers to a yes/no follow-up question (E12).
AnswerOption.title: AnswerOption

AnswerOutcome.description:
What a "yes" settles, where the step asking knows it: the class and, for high-risk, the
route, the provision and the date the duties apply from (decision 026 items 13 and 18). A
"no" has no such outcome: no class is predicted before the remaining checks run, so the
interface shows the fixed sentence of decision 026 item 13 instead.

provision_id.description: The provision a yes rests on, for example `annex:I:A:11`.
provision_id.title: Provision Id

duties_from.description: The date the route's high-risk duties apply from under the amended Art. 113 (the interface shows the original text's dates under it, decision 026 item 11); None when the AI Act itself sets no duties (an Annex I Section B product, Art. 2(2)).
duties_from.title: Duties From

AnswerOutcome.title: AnswerOutcome

Citation.description: One quoted provision. `english_only` marks guidance that has no official text in `de`.

document_id.description: The cited document's manifest `doc_key` (`data/manifest.yaml`), for example `ai-act-consolidated` or `guide-prohibited`; the citation checks resolve it against the corpus `documents.doc_key`.
document_id.title: Document Id

law_version.description: The AI Act text quoted; None for guidance, which belongs to neither text.

document_status.description: Lets draft guidance be labelled as a draft.

changed_by_omnibus.description: The quoted amended text is one the Digital Omnibus changed: the provision, a part of it or the provision it belongs to was replaced, inserted, deleted or amended (INIT > Corpus rules). Never set on the original text.
changed_by_omnibus.title: Changed By Omnibus

Citation.title: Citation

DocumentStatus.description: The status of a corpus document (matches F4's `documents.status`).
DocumentStatus.title: DocumentStatus

EvidenceTag.description: Where a fact came from; used instead of a numeric confidence score.
EvidenceTag.title: EvidenceTag

Fact.description: A fact about the system and where it came from. Only stated facts point into the text.
Fact.title: Fact

FollowUpQuestion.description: A key-fact question. Its `id` keys the user's answer when the engine runs again.

about.description: What the answer settles, for example a step or provision_id.
about.title: About

hint.description: Why the answer matters, naming the provision it decides, in the result's language.
hint.title: Hint

options.description: The answers offered: yes, no and not sure for a yes/no question; empty for a question answered in words.
options.title: Options

if_yes.description: What a yes settles, when the step knows it.

citations.description: The provisions the question rests on, quoted; on a step's missing fact, each is one of the step's own (checked) citations.
citations.title: Citations

FollowUpQuestion.title: FollowUpQuestion

HighRiskRoute.description: How a system became high-risk; the two routes have different dates (Art. 113(c)).
HighRiskRoute.title: HighRiskRoute

Language.description: The languages the assistant answers and quotes in.
Language.title: Language

LawText.description:
The AI Act text a result was checked against, as the screens label it ("the consolidated
AI Act of 27 July 2026", CELEX 02024R1689-20260727).

version_date.description: The original's publication date in the Official Journal, or the consolidation's cut-off date.
version_date.title: Version Date

LawText.title: LawText

LawVersion.description: The AI Act text a result relies on: as published in 2024, or as amended by the Omnibus.
LawVersion.title: LawVersion

LegacyStatus.description:
How Art. 111(2) treats a high-risk system placed on the market or put into service before
its route's Chapter III date, with no significant change planned from that date.
LegacyStatus.title: LegacyStatus

Obligation.description: One duty with its article reference and the date it applies from.

high_risk_route.description: The high-risk route `applies_from` belongs to; None when the date is the same for every route (or the class is not high-risk).

applies_if.description: The condition under which the duty applies; None when it applies to every system of this role and class.
applies_if.title: Applies If

is_informational.description: True when the row informs (e.g. a distributor of a prohibited system) rather than stating a formal duty the Act puts on this role.
is_informational.title: Is Informational

legacy.description: Art. 111(2) for a system on the market or in use before its route's date: `legacy_unchanged` means the duty applies only after a significant change to the system's design or purpose; `legacy_public_authority` means it applies from 2 Aug 2030 (`applies_from`). None when the system is not such a legacy system or the duty is not a high-risk one.

relief_note.description: Relief for SMEs, start-ups and small mid-caps (SMCs), if any.
relief_note.title: Relief Note

Obligation.title: Obligation

OpenQuestion.description: A question the law and guidance don't settle, with both possible readings.

readings.description: The two possible readings, stricter first; the stricter one is applied.
readings.title: Readings

settled_by.description: What would settle the question, when the step knows it.
settled_by.title: Settled By

OpenQuestion.title: OpenQuestion

Reading.description:
One possible reading of an open question of law (E12): what it is called, the class it
gives, why, the provision it rests on, and what follows if it holds.

title.description: None for a reading without its own title: a baseline's, or one stored before E12.
title.title: Title

risk_class.description: The class this reading gives on its own check, for example `high_risk` for the stricter reading of a high-risk question. None when it gives no class by itself: the remaining checks decide (shown as, for example, not high-risk on this point), or the question is about a duty or the role, not the class.

citation.description: The provision the reading rests on: one of its step's citations.

consequence.description: What follows if the reading holds.
consequence.title: Consequence

is_applied.description: The working assumption: the stricter reading, applied until a lawyer or the user's answer settles the question.
is_applied.title: Is Applied

Reading.title: Reading

RiskClass.description: The headline class. Every result carries exactly one.
RiskClass.title: RiskClass

Role.description: The operator role the obligations follow from (Art. 3, 16, 23-26).
Role.title: Role

SettledBy.description:
Something that would settle an open question. Guidance is named as it stands (for example
a draft); naming it never promises that the result is checked again (decision 026 item 4).
SettledBy.title: SettledBy

SettledByKind.description: What could settle an open question of law (E12, decision 026 item 4).
SettledByKind.title: SettledByKind

SourceSpan.description: Character offsets `[start, end)` of a fact in the user's description.
SourceSpan.title: SourceSpan

Status.description: Whether a step or result is settled. The two uncertain values are not risk classes.
Status.title: Status

StepName.description: The checks in the Act's fixed order (INIT > How it works).
StepName.title: StepName

StepResult.description: The outcome of one check. An uncertain status names what is missing or open.

missing_fact.description: The question that would supply the missing fact.

error.description: A machine-readable failure code, for example `citation_unverified`.
error.title: Error

StepResult.title: StepResult

description:
The engine's answer. When `status` is uncertain, `risk_class` is the stricter reading,
kept as the labelled working assumption.

role.description: Set exactly when the role_obligations step ran.

also_role.description: A role the company keeps next to `role`, whose duties are listed too: a deployer that becomes the provider still uses the system (shown as "You also use it").

role_switch_reason.description: Why the Art. 25 switch to provider applies, when it does.
role_switch_reason.title: Role Switch Reason

transparency_duties.description: Art. 50 provisions that apply, for example `art:50:1`.
transparency_duties.title: Transparency Duties

law_text.description: The label of the text `law_version` names (CELEX number and date); it always matches `law_version`, which sets it when it is left out.

legal_review.description: The recommendation to have the result reviewed by a lawyer, in the result's language: set for high-risk, prohibited and legally ambiguous results (INIT > Ethical considerations).
legal_review.title: Legal Review

not_assessed.description: The checks the model provider refused to assess (decision 029), in check order; each needs a person's review, and its stricter reading is assumed.
not_assessed.title: Not Assessed

title: ClassificationResult
